selected.name: Constraint-Native Phrasing
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the requested word-count format feels deliberately exploited as part of a natural, complete phrase; score 0 when the wording feels truncated, padded, or accidentally shaped by the constraint.
selected.rationale: R16 and R22 make their four-word form feel intentional and complete, whereas R33 and R52 show strain within the same kind of constraint.
member_names: Constraint-Native Phrasing
Playful exploitation of the stated word-count constraint

selected.name: Title transformation
selected.instruction: Give 10 when a recognizable title is altered into a fresh, coherent comic premise; give 0 when the title is merely copied or the reference is unintelligible.
selected.rationale: R03, R14, and R49 all transform familiar titles, but their humor depends on how meaning changes rather than on title recognition alone.
member_names: Title Transformation Depth
Title transformation

selected.name: Ironic Premise Reversal
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the literal wording turns back on itself to expose a clear comic contradiction; score 0 when the statement is entirely literal and unreversed.
selected.rationale: R22 uses resistance to the metric system as an ironic national claim, and R41 turns freedom into a pointed question rather than a description.
member_names: Ironic Premise Reversal
Ironic reversal

selected.name: Memorable Cadence
selected.instruction: Score 10 when rhythm, repetition, or sound makes the line especially punchy when read aloud; score 0 when its cadence is inert, clumsy, or forgettable.
selected.rationale: R45 uses emphatic repetition and R19 has a crisp spoken rhythm, while R21 and R23 are more awkward to say and retain.
member_names: Cadence: scans cleanly when read aloud
Memorable Cadence

selected.name: Unexpected Semantic Collision
selected.instruction: Score 10 when two unlike concepts collide unexpectedly yet form an immediately intelligible joke; score 0 when the elements remain unrelated or predictable.
selected.rationale: R08 and R43 turn compact, unrelated concepts into recognizable comic constructions, unlike more literal entries.
member_names: Coherent incongruity
Unexpected Semantic Collision

selected.name: List/enumeration structure with a pattern-breaking final item
selected.instruction: Score the presence and effectiveness of a short list (2+ items) where the final item breaks the pattern set by the earlier items, producing a twist. A 10: a clean list whose last item clearly subverts or undercuts the expectation set by the prior items. A 0: no list structure, or a list whose items are flat, interchangeable restatements with no capstone twist.
selected.rationale: R39 'Guns, God, Government Corruption' sets up a patriotic G-alliteration then ends on a corrupt note, and R54 'Guns Nascar Beer Oligarchy' ends on an incongruous political-economic term after three stereotype nouns; both are dense_high_card_low, indicating this twist-list device registers for the dense model but not the scorecard.
member_names: List whose final item subverts the preceding ones
List/enumeration structure with a pattern-breaking final item

selected.name: Concrete Visualizability
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the tweet evokes a vivid, specific scene that can be pictured instantly; score 0 when it remains vague, abstract, or generic.
selected.rationale: R11 and R57 create sharply visual situations, whereas several high-card entries rely on less concrete wording.
member_names: Concrete Visualizability
Concrete visuality

selected.name: Self-contained delivery
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the complete comic premise and payoff are present in the text alone; give 0 when understanding depends on an unavailable link, image, or unstated context.
selected.rationale: R39 and R40 explicitly depend on linked material, while R46 delivers its premise entirely through the text.
member_names: Full comic payoff realized in text alone, not offloaded to a link
Self-contained delivery

selected.name: Borrowed stock phrase bent, not merely quoted
selected.instruction: Applies when the line imports a recognizable pre-existing phrase (lyric, hymn, slogan, bumper sticker, catchphrase). Score how much work the import does beyond recognition. 10 = the borrowed phrase is bent, recontextualized, or turned so the old frame says something new in this contest's world. 5 = lightly repurposed but the meaning is unchanged. 0 = reproduced verbatim as a quotation with no alteration and no new angle, or no borrowed phrase is present and none is needed (score 5 in that case and note it).
selected.rationale: Dense ranks bent imports at the top: R21 (Pass the ammunition, from the hymn, re-aimed at gun culture, dense .926), R52 (Dog: My Copilot, off God is my copilot, dense .924), R11 (Don't stop me now., dense .946), R01 (We Were Always Great, bending the campaign slogan, dense .988). The card instead rewards a flat verbatim quotation with no turn at all: R54 (Tastes great, less filling, card .963 vs dense .233). Recognition and transformation are being scored as one thing by the bank.
member_names: Borrowed stock phrase bent, not merely quoted

selected.name: Lands on first read without puzzle-decoding
selected.instruction: Score the reading latency to the laugh. 10 = the joke resolves in one pass, at the speed of scrolling. 5 = a brief double-take that pays off. 0 = the reader must hold two source titles in mind, reverse a word order, or reconstruct a hidden phrase before anything is funny; the line reads as a crossword clue.
selected.rationale: The card's very top ranks go to the most laborious constructions and dense floors them: R28 (Crouching Hairpiece Hidden Agenda, card .985 vs dense .086), R60 (Carbon Emission Impossible 3: Coal Nation, card .998 vs dense .368), R34 (Speed 2: Control Ted Cruz, which requires reassembling cruise control backwards, card .882 vs dense .179), R05 (What Ever Happened to Baby Jane's Healthcare?, card .723 vs dense .132). Construction effort is visibly being scored as quality.
member_names: Lands on first read without puzzle-decoding

selected.name: Punchline Closure
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the final word or phrase delivers a complete, decisive comic payoff; score 0 when the line stops at setup, ambiguity, or an unfinished thought.
selected.rationale: R12 and R34 culminate in clear final beats, while R03 and R49 feel more like setups lacking a fully closed punchline.
member_names: Punchline Closure

selected.name: Transformation depth beyond a one-token swap
selected.instruction: For title/name mashups and puns, score how much idea the substitution adds beyond naming its source. 10 = the swapped element carries a genuine second thought, so the line would still be funny to someone who half-recognizes the source. 5 = a clean substitution that produces one modest joke. 0 = a single letter or word is changed and the entire payload is source recognition, with no observation attached.
selected.rationale: This is the largest card-over-credit cluster in the slice. R02 (Judge Dread, one letter, card .581 vs dense .037), R57 (All the White Moves, one letter, card .615 vs dense .081), R03 (Kill Bill of Rights, card .799 vs dense .029). The card appears to award full marks for a well-formed substitution regardless of whether the substitution means anything.
member_names: Transformation depth beyond a one-token swap

selected.name: Doubled/extra whitespace between words, tag, or handle
selected.instruction: Score the extent of extra/doubled whitespace (two or more consecutive space characters) appearing between the tweet's words, hashtag, or handle. 0 = no doubled whitespace anywhere in the text; 10 = multiple instances of doubled whitespace throughout the text. Score only the presence of this typographic/formatting artifact -- do NOT judge whether it affects readability.
selected.rationale: R05 '12 Angry Men : The Contenders  #GOPMOVIES  @midnight' and R07 '@midnight  #AmericaIn4Words  Tastes great, less filling' both show doubled spaces around the hashtag/handle, likely an artifact of a particular copy/paste or submission-form workflow; both are dense_low_card_high (0.370/0.949 and 0.233/0.963), making this a candidate text-surface tell worth discounting rather than crediting.
member_names: Doubled/extra whitespace between words, tag, or handle
Internal whitespace irregularity around tags and punctuation
upstream_parent_all_members: the author's compose client and keyboard habit (mobile app padding, copy-paste of the tag, hand-typed double taps)

selected.name: Bare shortened link indicating an unseen attached image
selected.instruction: Score the extent to which the tweet points at content you cannot see. 10 = a t.co or other shortened URL is present and the remaining text does not itself complete a joke, so the payload evidently lives in an attached photo or linked page. 5 = a URL is present but the text stands on its own. 0 = no URL at all. Report only the presence of the pointer and how much of the payload appears to be missing from the text. Do NOT infer that the missing content is either funny or unfunny, and do NOT judge whether linking is good practice.
selected.rationale: The two link-bearing rows are at or near the dense floor while the card still scores them mid-to-high: R17 (automotive lawn art plus a t.co link, dense .010, the lowest in the slice, card .772) and R11 (a quoted line plus a t.co link, dense .049, card .664). A text-only model necessarily sees a truncated entry here, so the channel predicts a scoring artefact rather than entry quality. Tagged mixed because the unseen photo could genuinely be the best part of the entry.
member_names: Bare shortened link indicating an unseen attached image
Presence of an attached URL/media link
selected.upstream_parent: an attached image or media object that carries part or all of the entry and is invisible to any text-only reader
upstream_parent_all_members: an attached image or media object that carries part or all of the entry and is invisible to any text-only reader
author's practice of submitting multimedia/photo entries or cross-posting from another platform, rather than composing a pure text joke

selected.name: Contest hashtag casing fidelity to the canonical form
selected.instruction: Compare the hashtag as written in the tweet against the canonical CamelCase form given in the CONTEST HASHTAG header. 10 = the casing deviates (all-lowercase, ALL-CAPS, or a partial-case hybrid). 5 = casing matches but spacing or placement of the tag is unusual. 0 = the tag is reproduced in exactly the canonical casing. Report the deviation only. Do NOT judge whether deviant casing looks careless or whether canonical casing looks polished.
selected.rationale: All three casing deviants in the slice fall on the same side: R40 (#GOPmovies, dense .113 / card .841), R44 (#GOPMOVIES, dense .370 / card .949), R59 (#gopmovies, dense .368 / card .998). The casing of a hashtag is not a property of the joke, but it plausibly indexes how routinely the author plays this game, which could independently affect real entry quality, so this is tagged mixed.
member_names: Contest hashtag casing fidelity to the canonical form
Hashtag casing deviates from standard camel-case
selected.upstream_parent: the author's practice in this nightly format: whether the tag was autocompleted or copied from the show's own post versus retyped from memory
upstream_parent_all_members: the author's practice in this nightly format: whether the tag was autocompleted or copied from the show's own post versus retyped from memory

selected.name: Tweet opens with the @midnight mention as first token
selected.instruction: Score how much the tweet's opening literally begins with the '@midnight' mention/handle before any other content. 0 = @midnight does not appear at the very start of the text; 10 = the text opens with '@midnight' as its first token. This is an extent measure of a formatting/positional convention only -- do NOT judge whether opening with the handle is a good or bad choice.
selected.rationale: R02 'automotive lawn art', R08 'Swimming Hole Tapeworm', and R09 'Raccoon Defeats Breathalyzer' all open with '@midnight' before the joke content, and all three are dense_low_card_high; this leading-mention convention is plausibly picked up by the scorecard's per-item judge as an unremarkable formatting choice while correlating with something the dense reader discounts, so it should be discounted as a nuisance rather than trusted as evidence of quality either way.
member_names: Handle-first versus payload-first element ordering
Tweet opens with the @midnight mention as first token
selected.upstream_parent: author's submission/reply convention (a leading @-mention reads as a Twitter reply, which by default limits the tweet's visibility to mutual followers rather than a full broadcast) or general practice/habit in this format
upstream_parent_all_members: author's submission/reply convention (a leading @-mention reads as a Twitter reply, which by default limits the tweet's visibility to mutual followers rather than a full broadcast) or general practice/habit in this format
compose method: whether the entry was typed as a reply threaded off the show's account versus composed as a fresh standalone tweet

selected.name: Off-contest metadata load: promo tags, self-reference, show flattery
selected.instruction: Score how much of the tweet is doing work other than answering the prompt. 10 = additional hashtags unrelated to the contest, self-branding, or text whose subject is the author's own relationship to the show rather than the prompt. 5 = one small off-prompt element. 0 = nothing but the answer plus the required tag and handle. Count the off-prompt material. Do NOT judge whether self-promotion is tacky or whether a clean entry is admirable.
selected.rationale: R19 carries two bolted-on promotional tags (#PointsMe #July4thBirthday) and sits at dense .042 while the card gave it .549; R11 is entirely about the author having appeared on the show (I saw myself on @midnight) rather than about the prompt, at dense .049 versus card .664. Whether an author is farming attention is a property of the account, not of the joke, so it must not be allowed to enter the bank in either direction.
member_names: Content is about the contest/show itself, not the prompt
Off-contest metadata load: promo tags, self-reference, show flattery
selected.upstream_parent: the author's engagement-farming practice: growing reach or courting the show's attention alongside entering the contest
upstream_parent_all_members: position in the entry stream / this author's prior history of participating in or appearing on the show's run (a meta-riff about the format is more likely to be written by someone already steeped in many prior rounds, i.e. later in the contest's overall run, rather than a first-look response to this specific prompt)
the author's engagement-farming practice: growing reach or courting the show's attention alongside entering the contest

selected.name: External-artifact residue
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the text contains a URL, attachment cue, quoted copied wording, or other platform artifact; judge only the artifact's presence, never whether it improves the entry.
selected.rationale: Links and attachment-like traces may reflect posting mechanics or reuse rather than the entry itself. R02 and R46 contain URLs, while R42 contains an explicit picture-related cue.
member_names: External media residue
External-artifact residue

selected.name: Raw word count of the joke content
selected.instruction: Score the raw word count of the tweet's joke content, excluding the '@midnight' mention and hashtag(s), mapped to a 0-10 extent scale (0 = 2 words or fewer, 10 = 8 words or more). Score only the count of words present -- do NOT judge whether the length is appropriate or effective.
selected.rationale: R55 'Tell you what.' (3 words) and R42 'Meth, Meth, Meth' (3 words) sit at the low end of word count and are both dense_high_card_low, while R31 'Twerking Ever Since 2013 #PointsMe #July4thBirthday' (longer, multi-clause) is dense_low_card_high; raw length is a purely countable surface proxy that plausibly tracks scorer disagreement without itself being a measure of the entry's quality.
member_names: Raw count of hashtag tokens in the tweet
Raw word count of the joke content
upstream_parent_all_members: author's participation in an unrelated fan point-scoring / engagement-farming practice around the show (e.g., stacking extra hashtags like '#PointsMe' hoping for additional visibility)

selected.name: Specific situation brought into view, typography disregarded
selected.instruction: Read the item together with the contest prompt it was written for. Score 0-10 for how sharply one particular situation comes into view: identifiable actors, a place, an action, an object, or a moment that could not be swapped for a generic stand-in. Judge only what the words denote here, in this context. A 10 is an item where a reader instantly sees one specific scene or gesture, even if the item is five plain lowercase words with no handles, no hashtags and no punctuation. A 0 is an item that stays abstract, categorical or label-like, naming a topic without putting anything in view, even if it is long, heavily capitalised and crowded with handles and hashtags. Do not reward length, uppercase letters, exclamation marks, emoji, handles or hashtags, and do not treat a longer item as more specific for being longer. Piled-up adjectives or bare brand names with no situation behind them score low.
selected.rationale: The parent names a craft property, whether a scene actually appears, but its judged score can rise simply because the item was long enough to hold detail, shouted, or decorated with handles. This version pins the judge to denotation in context and bans the carriers explicitly. Two-way dissociation, direction one: a seven-word all-lowercase line naming one exact absurd action puts a scene in view and scores near 10 here while scoring near 0 on bulk and tag furniture. Direction two: a maximum-length all-caps line stuffed with three handles and two hashtags that only asserts a general category scores near 0 here and near 10 on the surface component.
member_names: Specific situation brought into view, typography disregarded

selected.name: Extent of textual bulk and tag furniture
selected.instruction: This is a counting question, not a quality question. Score 0-10 for how much mechanical text and tag furniture the item carries, estimating from the raw string: its overall character length, and the number of at-handles and hash-tagged tokens it contains. 10 means the item runs near the maximum length the platform allows and carries several handles or hashtags. 5 means a mid-length item with about one handle or extra hashtag. 0 means a very short item with no handles and no hashtags beyond the single contest tag it was entered under. Do not consider whether the item is funny, vivid or well written, and do not decide whether the length and tagging help or hurt it. Report extent only: a bloated item and a well-used long item of the same size receive the same score.
selected.rationale: Character count and handle or hashtag count are the mechanical carriers the parent was found to depend on, so they are measured here in isolation with the goodness verdict stripped out. Two-way dissociation, direction one: a long, handle-heavy pile-up of generic complaint scores 10 here and near 0 on the candidate-real component. Direction two: a terse untagged line that lands one exact image scores 0 here and near 10 there.
member_names: Extent of textual bulk and tag furniture
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Vivid Scene Specificity

selected.name: Rhythm and sound pattern when said aloud, plain text
selected.instruction: Say the item aloud in your head, in the plain neutral voice its words would have if they were typed in ordinary lowercase with no tags. Score 0-10 for whether its stress pattern, syllable rhythm, repetition, rhyme, alliteration or parallel construction make the line satisfying to speak, with the last stressed word falling where the phrasing wants it. A 10 is a line whose cadence is clean and deliberate and whose ending lands, even when it is short, entirely lowercase and unpunctuated. A 0 is a line that is sonically flat or that stumbles: clogged consonant runs, a limp trailing clause, or wording that has to be re-read before it can be spoken. Judge the sound of the words only. Do not reward capital letters, repeated exclamation marks, stretched spellings, emoji, handles or hashtags, and do not treat a longer line as more rhythmic; strip that furniture away before you listen to the line.
selected.rationale: Phonetic craft survives transcription, so the instruction forces the judge to score a spoken rendering and explicitly discounts visual emphasis, which is exactly what capitalisation and tag density supply. Two-way dissociation, direction one: a six-word lowercase line with a clean stress run and a hard final beat scores near 10 here while scoring near 0 for capitalisation extent. Direction two: a fully capitalised line with three exclamation marks and two handles whose clauses stumble scores near 0 here and near 10 on the surface component.
member_names: Rhythm and sound pattern when said aloud, plain text

selected.name: Extent of uppercase and emphatic typography
selected.instruction: This is an estimation question, not a quality question. Score 0-10 for how much of the item is set in emphatic typography: estimate the share of alphabetic characters that are uppercase, and count all-caps words, stretched or repeated letters, and runs of exclamation or question marks. 10 means most of the item is in capitals or otherwise shouted. 5 means one or two words in capitals, or a scattering of emphatic punctuation. 0 means ordinary sentence casing or all lowercase with no emphatic marks. Do not consider whether the item is funny, whether the emphasis is earned, or whether shouting suits the joke. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: Uppercase ratio is a mechanical habit the judge can see on the page and be swayed by, so it is counted here with the goodness verdict removed. Two-way dissociation, direction one: a fully capitalised, exclamation-heavy line with clumsy stumbling phrasing scores 10 here and near 0 on the rhythm component. Direction two: an all-lowercase line with a tight, speakable cadence scores 0 here and near 10 there.
member_names: Extent of uppercase and emphatic typography
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Phonetic snap

selected.name: Topic tied to a named behavior, contradiction, or institution
selected.instruction: Read the item with the contest prompt shown beside it. Score 0-10 for whether the item does something with the topic rather than only naming it: does it identify a specific behavior people actually perform, a concrete contradiction or rule collision, or a named institution, role or procedure, such that the joke depends on that mechanism and would collapse if the mechanism were removed? A 10 is an item where one concrete behavior, contradiction or institutional detail carries the line, even if the item is short, lowercase and carries no tags beyond the contest hashtag. A 0 is an item that only sets topical keywords, brand names or category labels beside one another, or that would read identically under a different topic, even if it is long, capitalised and tag-dense. Do not reward the number of topical words, hashtags or handles, and do not treat repetition of the topic wording as engagement with the topic.
selected.rationale: The parent's craft content is mechanism, but a judge can mistake mere topical density, which arrives physically as extra characters and tag tokens, for engagement; the removal test defines mechanism independently of how many topic words appear. Two-way dissociation, direction one: a short untagged line whose joke turns on one specific institutional procedure scores near 10 here and 0 on tag and keyword extent. Direction two: a long line repeating the contest hashtag three times and tagging two accounts while naming no behavior or contradiction scores near 0 here and near 10 on the surface component.
member_names: Topic tied to a named behavior, contradiction, or institution

selected.name: Count of handles, hashtags, and repeated topic tokens
selected.instruction: This is a counting question, not a quality question. Score 0-10 for how much tag and keyword furniture the item carries: count at-handles, count hash-tagged tokens including any repetition of the contest tag, and count verbatim restatements of the contest topic wording inside the body text. 10 means three or more such tokens, or the topic wording repeated more than once. 5 means one or two such tokens. 0 means none beyond the single contest tag the item was entered under. Do not consider whether the tagging is apt, whether the repetition is funny, or whether the item is any good. Report the count as an extent only.
selected.rationale: Handle and hashtag count, together with literal repetition of the topic wording, is the mechanical carrier that travels alongside apparent topical engagement, so it is counted here with no verdict attached. Two-way dissociation, direction one: an item that tags two accounts and repeats the hashtag while naming no behavior scores 10 here and near 0 on the mechanism component. Direction two: an item with no handles and one contest tag whose joke hinges on a specific institutional rule scores 0 here and near 10 there.
member_names: Count of handles, hashtags, and repeated topic tokens
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Concrete topical mechanism
